title: Course Schedule
summary: Decide whether a set of prerequisites can be satisfied at all.
statement:
There are `n` courses numbered `0` to `n - 1`. Each entry `[a, b]` of `prerequisites` means course `b` must be taken before course `a`.

Return `true` if every course can be completed, and `false` otherwise.

### Constraints

- 1 ≤ n ≤ 5,000
- 0 ≤ prerequisites.length ≤ 10,000
- Duplicate pairs may appear

### Example

```
n = 2, prerequisites = [[1, 0]]        -> true   (take 0, then 1)
n = 2, prerequisites = [[1, 0], [0, 1]] -> false  (each needs the other)
```

> **What makes it impossible**
>
> Exactly one thing: a cycle in the prerequisite graph. So this is a cycle-detection question wearing a timetable costume. Either peel off courses with no remaining prerequisites until none are left (Kahn's algorithm), or depth-first search while tracking the nodes on the current path.
>
> A node already finished is not a cycle — only one still on the stack is.
